title: Learning single-cell perturbation responses using neural optimal transport

nodes.text: CellOT is a framework that learns single-cell perturbation responses by recovering an optimal transport map between unpaired distributions of control and perturbed cells, one map per perturbation.
nodes.evidence: CellOT, a framework for learning the response of individual cells to a given perturbation by mapping these unpaired distributions

nodes.text: Rather than directly parameterizing the OT map (which is unstable), CellOT parameterizes the dual convex potentials with input convex neural networks and recovers the map as the gradient of a learned convex potential ∇g_k.
nodes.evidence: we parameterize the convex potentials of the dual optimal transport problem f and g by input convex neural networks and recover the optimal map Tk using the gradient of a convex function gk

nodes.text: Using input convex neural networks for the dual potentials induces a theory-motivated inductive bias essential to model stability, distinguishing CellOT from directly learning a transport map.
nodes.evidence: This choice induces an important theory-motivated inductive bias essential to model stability

nodes.text: Unlike prior OT-based single-cell methods that are non-parameterized and cannot predict on unseen cells, CellOT learns a fully parameterized, scalable map that can forecast perturbation outcomes for previously unseen control cells and new patients.
nodes.evidence: current OT-based approaches are unable to make predictions on unseen cells... CellOT learns an optimal transport map for each perturbation in a fully parameterized and highly scalable manner

nodes.text: Current state-of-the-art autoencoder methods (scGEN, cAE) predict responses via linear shifts in a learned latent space and tend to capture only the mean of the perturbed population, learning over-simplified perturbation effects.
nodes.evidence: Current state-of-the-art methods predict perturbation responses via linear shifts in a learned latent space... these models tend to learn over-simplified perturbation effects

nodes.text: CellOT outperforms autoencoder baselines scGEN and cAE and the PopAlign method at predicting single-cell drug responses, typically by one order of magnitude on MMD and l2-mean metrics across all treatments.
nodes.evidence: CellOT outperforms the baselines in both metrics across all treatments, typically by one order of magnitude

nodes.text: CellOT captures higher moments of the perturbed cell population (not just the mean) and can approach the observed-data lower bound, whereas baseline methods often do not improve much over the trivial identity baseline.
nodes.evidence: CellOT can approach the lower bound (observed setting), whereas the baseline methods often do not improve much over the identity setting

nodes.text: CellOT generalizes to unseen settings: predicting holdout lupus patients' scRNA-seq responses to interferon-beta and glioblastoma patients' responses to panobinostat, inferring LPS responses across species, and modeling hematopoietic developmental trajectories.
nodes.evidence: predicting the scRNA-seq responses of holdout patients with lupus exposed to interferon-β and patients with glioblastoma to panobinostat; (2) inferring lipopolysaccharide responses across different species; and (3) modeling the hematopoietic developmental trajectories

nodes.text: Predicted and observed perturbed cells had near-identical UMAP spatial organization and highly comparable pERK distributions across drug treatments, indicating CellOT preserves the link between signaling-kinase phosphorylation and cellular state.
nodes.evidence: the spatial organization of the two projections looked almost identical and that pERK levels had a highly comparable distribution

nodes.text: CellOT is free of the limitations of label-guided or mean-response methods (reliance on predefined cell-type labels and the assumption of uniform within-type response), enabling discovery of cell-state-specific perturbation responses.
nodes.evidence: CellOT is free of these limitations and enables scientists to query the predicted single-cell responses at the granularity best suited

nodes.text: Strong OT performance is attributed to the inter-feature correlation structure remaining largely conserved between treated and untreated populations, a setting where OT approaches excel.
nodes.evidence: the inter-feature correlation structure remains largely conserved between treated and untreated populations, thus depicting a setting where OT approaches excel

nodes.text: CellOT disentangles subpopulation-specific drug effects by computing the difference between predicted perturbed and untreated control cells, producing distinct treatment embeddings absent when only an average perturbation effect is modeled.
nodes.evidence: Such distinct treatment embeddings are not present when accounting only for an average perturbation effect
